InvisiMole can use zlib to compress and decompress data.
InvisiMole uses variations of a simple XOR encryption routine for C&C communications.
InvisiMole can function as a proxy to create a server that relays communication between the client and C&C server, or between two clients.
InvisiMole lists local users and session information.
InvisiMole can collect data from the system, and can monitor changes in specified directories.
InvisiMole can launch a remote shell to execute commands.
InvisiMole can enumerate Registry values, keys, and data.
InvisiMole can mimic HTTP protocol with custom HTTP “verbs” HIDE, ZVVP, and NOP.
InvisiMole can capture screenshots of not only the entire screen, but of each separate window open, in case they are overlapping.
InvisiMole can collect information about installed software used by specific users, software executed on user login, and software executed by each system.
InvisiMole can remotely activate the victim’s webcam to capture content.
InvisiMole can decrypt, unpack and load a DLL from its resources, or from blobs encrypted with Data Protection API, two-key triple DES, and variations of the XOR cipher.
InvisiMole gathers the local system time from the victim’s machine.
InvisiMole can gather information on the mapped drives and system volume serial number.
InvisiMole has been configured with several servers available for alternate C2 communications.
InvisiMole can enumerate windows and child windows on a compromised host.
InvisiMole uses WinRAR to compress data that is intended to be exfiltrated.
InvisiMole can obtain running services on the victim.
InvisiMole has disguised its droppers as legitimate software or documents, matching their original names and locations, and saved its files as mpr.dll in the Windows folder.
InvisiMole can record sound using input audio devices.
InvisiMole uses HTTP for C2 communications.
InvisiMole can use fileless UAC bypass and create an elevated COM object to escalate privileges.
InvisiMole has a command to create, set, copy, or delete a specified Registry key or value.
InvisiMole uses a variation of the XOR cipher to encrypt files before exfiltration.
InvisiMole has deleted files and directories including XML and files successfully uploaded to C2 servers.
InvisiMole can obtain a list of running processes.
InvisiMole can disconnect previously connected remote drives.
InvisiMole can sort and collect specific documents as well as generate a list of all files on a newly inserted drive and store them in an encrypted file.
InvisiMole can gather network share information.
InvisiMole avoids analysis by encrypting all strings, internal files, configuration data and by using a custom executable format.
InvisiMole samples were timestomped by the authors by setting the PE timestamps to all zero values. InvisiMole also has a built-in command to modify file times.
InvisiMole determines a working directory where it stores all the gathered data about the compromised machine.
InvisiMole can gather information on the OS version, computer name, DEP policy, and memory size.
ref-2115266458f656333846.title: Hromcová, Z. (2018, June 07). InvisiMole: Surprisingly equipped spyware, undercover since 2013. Retrieved July 10, 2018.

ref-2e5ce0b63b29a50bf2af.text: Raspberry Robin uses rundll32 execution without any command line parameters to contact command and control infrastructure, such as IP addresses associated with Tor nodes. Raspberry Robin retrieves its second stage payload in a variety of ways such as through msiexec.exe abuse, or running the curl command to download the payload to the victim's %AppData% folder. Raspberry Robin uses newly-registered domains containing only a few characters for command and controll purposes, such as "v0[.]cx". Raspberry Robin uses regsvr32.exe execution without any command line parameters for command and control requests to IP addresses associated with Tor nodes. Raspberry Robin uses mixed-case letters for filenames and commands to evade detection. Raspberry Robin uses msiexec.exe for post-installation communication to command and control infrastructure. Msiexec.exe is executed referencing a remote resource for second-stage payload retrieval and execution. Raspberry Robin uses the Windows utility odbcconf.exe to execute malicious commands, using the regsvr flag to execute DLLs and bypass application control mechanisms that are not monitoring for odbcconf.exe abuse. Raspberry Robin is capable of contacting the TOR network for delivering second-stage payloads. Raspberry Robin has historically been delivered via infected USB drives containing a malicious LNK object masquerading as a legitimate folder. Raspberry Robin uses cmd.exe to read and execute a file stored on an infected USB device as part of initial installation. Raspberry Robin will communicate via HTTP over port 8080 for command and control traffic. Raspberry Robin uses outbound HTTP requests containing victim information for retrieving second stage payloads. Variants of Raspberry Robin can download archive files (such as 7-Zip files) via the victim web browser for second stage execution. Raspberry Robin has historically used infected USB media to spread to new victims. Raspberry Robin will use the legitimate Windows utility fodhelper.exe to run processes at elevated privileges without requiring a User Account Control prompt.
ref-2e5ce0b63b29a50bf2af.title: Lauren Podber and Stef Rand. (2022, May 5). Raspberry Robin gets the worm early. Retrieved May 17, 2024.

ref-36b1db959a3ca9db4f76.text:
Mispadu decrypts its encrypted configuration files prior to execution.
Mispadu can run checks to verify if it is running within a virtualized environments including Hyper-V, VirtualBox or VMWare and will terminate execution if the computer name is “JOHN-PC.”
Mispadu can steal credentials from Google Chrome.
Mispadu's binary is injected into memory via `WriteProcessMemory`.
Mispadu can monitor browser activity for online banking actions and display full-screen overlay images to block user access to the intended site or present additional data fields.
Mispadu uses a custom algorithm to obfuscate its internal strings and uses hardcoded keys. Mispadu also uses encoded configuration files and has encoded payloads using Base64.
Mispadu has obtained credentials from mail clients via NirSoft MailPassView.
Mispadu can sends the collected financial data to the C2 server.
Mispadu has been spread via malicious links embedded in emails.
Mispadu’s dropper uses VBS files to install payloads and perform execution.
Mispadu has been installed via MSI installer.
Mispadu checks and will terminate execution if the compromised system’s language ID is not Spanish or Portuguese.
Mispadu has relied on users to execute malicious files in order to gain execution on victim machines.
Mispadu has used a variety of Windows API calls, including ShellExecute and WriteProcessMemory.
Mispadu has the ability to capture screenshots on compromised hosts.
ref-36b1db959a3ca9db4f76.title: SCILabs. (2021, December 23). Cyber Threat Profile Malteiro. Retrieved March 13, 2024.

ref-3fc13a572854c2d18a1a.text: CHOPSTICK provides access to the Windows Registry, which can be used to gather information. CORESHELL C2 messages are encrypted with custom stream ciphers using six-byte or eight-byte keys. OLDBAIT can use SMTP for C2. CORESHELL contains unused machine instructions in a likely attempt to hinder analysis. CORESHELL collects the volume serial number from the victim and sends the information to its C2 server. OLDBAIT installs itself in %ALLUSERPROFILE%\\Application Data\Microsoft\MediaPlayer\updatewindws.exe; the directory name is missing a space and the file name is missing the letter "o." CORESHELL downloads another dropper from its C2 server. OLDBAIT collects credentials from Internet Explorer, Mozilla Firefox, and Eudora. CHOPSTICK may store RC4 encrypted configuration information in the Windows Registry. OLDBAIT collects credentials from several email clients. CORESHELL obfuscates strings using a custom stream cipher. CHOPSTICK checks for antivirus and forensics software. CORESHELL C2 messages are Base64-encoded. CORESHELL collects hostname and OS version data from the victim and sends the information to its C2 server. OLDBAIT obfuscates internal strings and unpacks them at startup. OLDBAIT can use HTTP for C2. CHOPSTICK includes runtime checks to identify an analysis environment and prevent execution on it.
ref-3fc13a572854c2d18a1a.title: FireEye. (2015). APT28: A WINDOW INTO RUSSIA’S CYBER ESPIONAGE OPERATIONS?. Retrieved August 19, 2015.

ref-491c288f0b79d4d64b99.text:
RansomHub can use Elliptic Curve Encryption to encrypt files on targeted systems. RansomHub can also skip content at regular intervals (ex. encrypt 1 MB, skip 3 MB) to optomize performance and enable faster encryption for large files.
RansomHub has placed a ransom note on comrpomised systems to warn victims and provide directions for how to retrieve data.
RansomHub has used `vssadmin.exe` to delete volume shadow copies.
RansomHub can stop processes associated with files currently in use to maximize the impact of encryption.
ref-491c288f0b79d4d64b99.title: CISA et al. (2024, August 29). #StopRansomware: RansomHub Ransomware. Retrieved March 17, 2025.

ref-4e26068add8fd4e011f6.text:
Mini Shai-Hulud has the ability to check system details for its language configuration and terminates actions when the system is configured for the Russian language.
Mini Shai-Hulud has utilized container administration commands to gather details of compromised hosts and gather credentials to include Kubernetes command-line utilities `kubectl get secrets`.
Mini Shai-Hulud has utilized Python scripts to execute payloads.
Mini Shai-Hulud has gathered and downloaded data stored on both compromised and publicly accessible code repositories.
Mini Shai-Hulud has accessed and propagated to AWS EC2 instances via SSM Send-Command.
ref-4e26068add8fd4e011f6.title: Webb, M. (2026, May 20). TeamPCP Wave Four: GitHub Breach via Poisoned VS Code Extension, durabletask PyPI Worm, and ~4,000 Internal Repositories Exfiltrated. Retrieved July 16, 2026.

ref-50ac67db20ca3fcf1cf9.text:
WhisperGate can deobfuscate downloaded files stored in reverse byte order and decrypt embedded resources using multiple XOR operations.
WhisperGate has used the `ExitWindowsEx` to flush file buffers to disk and stop running processes and other API calls.
WhisperGate can download and execute AdvancedRun.exe to disable the Windows Defender Theat Protection service and set an exclusion path for the C:\ drive.
WhisperGate can delete tools from a compromised host after execution.
WhisperGate can overwrite the Master Book Record (MBR) on victim systems with a malicious 16-bit bootloader.
WhisperGate can download additional stages of malware from a Discord CDN channel.
WhisperGate can use a Visual Basic script to exclude the `C:\` drive from Windows Defender.
WhisperGate can download additional payloads hosted on a Discord channel.
WhisperGate can use PowerShell to support multiple actions including execution and defense evasion.
WhisperGate can shutdown a compromised host through execution of `ExitWindowsEx` with the `EXW_SHUTDOWN` flag.
WhisperGate can overwrite sectors of a victim host's hard drive at periodic offsets.
WhisperGate can enumerate connected remote logical drives.
WhisperGate can corrupt files by overwriting the first 1 MB with `0xcc` and appending random extensions.
WhisperGate overwrites the MBR with a bootloader component that performs destructive wiping operations on hard drives and displays a fake ransom note when the host boots.
WhisperGate has the ability to enumerate fixed logical drives on a targeted system.
WhisperGate can Base64 encode strings, store downloaded files in reverse byte order, and use the Eazfuscator tool to obfuscate its third stage.
The WhisperGate third stage can use the AdvancedRun.exe tool to execute commands in the context of the Windows TrustedInstaller group via `%TEMP%\AdvancedRun.exe" /EXEFilename "C:\Windows\System32\sc.exe" /WindowState 0 /CommandLine "stop WinDefend" /StartDirectory "" /RunAs 8 /Run`.
WhisperGate has the ability to inject its fourth stage into a suspended process created by the legitimate Windows utility `InstallUtil.exe`.
WhisperGate can locate files based on hardcoded file extensions.
ref-50ac67db20ca3fcf1cf9.title: Biasini, N. et al.. (2022, January 21). Ukraine Campaign Delivers Defacement and Wipers, in Continued Escalation. Retrieved March 14, 2022.

ref-6a0a65ba68e9965f0dc5.text: HyperStack can enumerate all account names on a remote share. Kazuar has used internal nodes on the compromised network for C2 communications. HyperStack can connect to the IPC$ share on remote machines. Carbon decrypts task and configuration files for execution. HyperStack can add the name of its communication pipe to HKLM\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\lanmanserver\\parameters\NullSessionPipes. HyperStack has used RSA encryption for C2 communications. Carbon encrypts configuration files and tasks for the malware to complete using CAST-128 algorithm. HyperStack can use default credentials to connect to IPC$ shares on remote machines. Carbon can use Pastebin to receive C2 commands. HyperStack can use Windows API's ConnectNamedPipe and WNetAddConnection2 to detect incoming connections and connect to remote shares. Carbon has used RSA encryption for C2 communications. Carbon can use HTTP in C2 communications.
ref-6a0a65ba68e9965f0dc5.title: Accenture. (2020, October). Turla uses HyperStack, Carbon, and Kazuar to compromise government entity. Retrieved December 2, 2020.

ref-995b74688fdbf73784d2.text:
PureCrypter can decrypt downloaded resources and parse internal files to determine its settings.
HeartCrypt can pack malicious Windows x86 and .NET payloads in order to evade detection.
PureCrypter can download additional payloads for execution on the compromised host.
PureCrypter can maintain persistence with scheduled tasks.
PureCrypter can execute PowerShell commands to exclude files from EDR and to self-delete.
PureCrypter can enumerate a targeted system's SerialNumber and Version.
PureCrypter has used SmartAssembly and NET-Reactor for string encryption and control flow obfuscation.
PureCrypter can set `ProcessWindowStyle.Hidden` to hide windows on victim machines.
HeartCrypt can decrypt payloads prior to execution.
PureCrypter can retrieve the username from targeted machines.
PureCrypter can identify installed antivirus solutions.
PureCrypter can use AES to encrypt system information sent to the C2.
PureCrypter can enumerate processes on compromised hosts.
ref-995b74688fdbf73784d2.title: Check Point Research. (2025, March 10). Blind Eagle: …And Justice for All. Retrieved April 16, 2026.

ref-a85398c0fe4dd2e669e9.text: Industroyer can use an arbitrary system service to load at system boot for persistence and replaces the ImagePath registry value of a Windows service with a new backdoor binary. Industroyer’s data wiper module clears registry keys and overwrites both ICS configuration and Windows files. Industroyer used Tor nodes for C2. Industroyer attempts to perform an HTTP CONNECT via an internal proxy to establish a tunnel. Industroyer collects the victim machine’s Windows GUID. Industroyer’s data wiper module writes zeros into the registry keys in SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services to render a system inoperable.
ref-a85398c0fe4dd2e669e9.title: Dragos Inc.. (2017, June 13). CRASHOVERRIDE Analysis of the Threat to Electric Grid Operations. Retrieved December 18, 2020.

ref-bc0367492d7779c139e0.text: DarkGate tries to elevate privileges to SYSTEM using PsExec to locally execute as a service, such as cmd /c c:\temp\PsExec.exe -accepteula -j -d -s [Target Binary]. DarkGate use Nirsoft Network Password Recovery or NetPass tools to steal stored RDP credentials in some malware versions. DarkGate relies on parent PID spoofing as part of its "rootkit-like" functionality to evade detection via Task Manager or Process Explorer. DarkGate includes one infection vector that leverages a malicious "KeyScramblerE.DLL" library that will load during the execution of the legitimate KeyScrambler application. DarkGate masquerades malicious LNK files as PDF objects using the double extension .pdf.lnk. DarkGate is distributed in phishing emails containing links to distribute malicious VBS or MSI files. DarkGate uses applications such as Microsoft Teams for distributing links to payloads. DarkGate command and control includes hard-coded domains in the malware masquerading as legitimate services such as Akamai CDN or Amazon Web Services. DarkGate checks the BeingDebugged flag in the PEB structure during execution to identify if the malware is being debugged. DarkGate command and control includes hard-coded domains in the malware chosen to masquerade as legitimate services such as Akamai CDN or Amazon Web Services. DarkGate executes a Windows Batch script during installation that creases a randomly-named directory in the C:\\ root directory that copies and renames the legitimate Windows curl command to this new location. DarkGate uses per-victim links for hosting malicious archives, such as ZIP files, in services such as SharePoint to prevent other entities from retrieving them. DarkGate uses a hard-coded string as a seed, along with the victim machine hardware identifier and input text, to generate a unique string used as an internal mutex value to evade static detection based on mutexes.
ref-bc0367492d7779c139e0.title: Ernesto Fernández Provecho, Pham Duy Phuc, Ciana Driscoll & Vinoo Thomas. (2023, November 21). The Continued Evolution of the DarkGate Malware-as-a-Service. Retrieved February 9, 2024.

ref-d074c16e14e4172c6256.text:
Bad Rabbit enumerates open SMB shares on internal victim networks.
Bad Rabbit has used Mimikatz to harvest credentials from the victim's machine.
Bad Rabbit has used various Windows API calls.
ref-d074c16e14e4172c6256.title: M.Léveille, M-E.. (2017, October 24). Bad Rabbit: Not‑Petya is back with improved ransomware. Retrieved January 28, 2021.

ref-eebcf489f6d2b5b685b6.text:
RansomHub has created an autorun Registry key through the `-safeboot-instance -pass` command line argument.
RansomHub can use a proxy to connect to remote SFTP servers.
RansomHub can use `cmd.exe` to execute multiple commands on infected hosts.
RansomHub will terminate without proceeding to encryption if the infected machine is on a list of allowlisted machines specified in its configuration.
RansomHub can retrieve information about virtual machines.
RansomHub can use credentials provided in its configuration to move laterally from the infected machine over SMBv2.
RansomHub has the ability to self-delete.
RansomHub can use a provided passphrase to decrypt its configuration file.
RansomHub has an encrypted configuration file.
RansomHub has the ability to terminate specified services.
RansomHub can sleep for a set number of minutes before beginning execution.
RansomHub can enumerate all accessible machines from the infected system.
RansomHub has the ability to target specific network shares for encryption.
RansomHub can delete events from the Security, System, and Application logs.
RansomHub can use PowerShell to delete volume shadow copies.
RansomHub can reboot targeted systems into Safe Mode prior to encryption.
RansomHub has the ability to only encrypt specific files.
ref-eebcf489f6d2b5b685b6.title: Alfano, V. et al. (2025, February 12). RansomHub Never Sleeps Episode 1: The evolution of modern ransomware. Retrieved March 17, 2025.
